summary: Cracked the maze DECORATION-SELECTION law (the special4 +0x1f8 / orient2 +0x378 planes -> wall SHAPE CODE) byte-exact from static disasm of the front/side classifier classify_front_side @0x3828 + the 16-way special4 jump table at FILE 0x3bc5 (jmp word cs:[bx-0x7ed7], bx=special4*2, overlay delta 0x4564). Decoration emit is GATED by orient2==facing (file 0x3af1). special4 indexes a 16-entry table to a shape code 4..0xe written into the per-(depth,slot) walltype array [0x5220] and fed to wall_emit_quad/corner. IDENTIFIED THE FOUNTAIN: special4==7 (shape code 4) — the gx126 gy118..121 column in level-0 region 0 (all orient2==0, decorates the facing-0/north face), the repeated side-wall fixture the party walks past entering the dungeon. The selection is now generated (generateDecorations / decorationShapeCode in packages/parser/src/maze/callist.ts) and gated by packages/parser/tests/maze/maze-decoration-parity.test.ts. The shape-code -> mazedata.ega placement-blit translation runs through the decompiler-resistant span-flush piece table (0x36e4 / wall_emit_quad 0x406c) and a live fountain-facing capture is BLOCKED by the documented serialize round-trip / poke-recompose tooling gap (maze-piece-inventory.json) — so it stays documented residue, NOT fabricated OR indices.

findings.claim: Decoration emit is gated by `orient2 == facing`. The classifier always reads special4 (+0x1f8) into [bp-6] and orient2 (+0x378) into [bp-8] after the wall-edge read, then enters the special4 dispatch iff (orient2==facing) || (special4==6) || (special4<=0xc). For special4==0 the table entry is a no-op (the raw wall field stands), so a plain cell is unchanged; the dispatch only changes the rendered FACE when orient2==facing selects the decorated face. For ALL level-0 decoration cells orient2==0, so decorations render only when facing 0 (north). This is the mechanical root of the user's 'fountains at the wrong angle' complaint.

evidence.details: 0x3acf reads +0x1f8 (special4, into [bp-6]); 0x3ae4 reads +0x378 (orient2, into [bp-8]); 0x3af1 `cmp ax(orient2),[0x4f9a](facing); je 0x3b06`; 0x3af7 `cmp [bp-6],6; je 0x3b06`; 0x3afd `cmp [bp-6],0xc; jg 0x3b06`; 0x3b03 `jmp 0x3bf2` (no-dispatch path). 0x3b06: `mov ax,[bp-6](special4); jmp 0x3be5` (the special4 dispatch). Confirmed via tools/parity/maze_disasm.py 0x3a40 0x1b0.

findings.claim: The 16-way special4 jump table at FILE 0x3bc5 maps special4 -> wall SHAPE CODE: 1->5, 2->6, 3->8, 4->9, 5->0xe, 7->4, 8->7, 9->0xa, 0xa->0xb, 0xb->0xc, 0xc->0xd. special4==0 -> no-op (raw wall field stands). special4==6 sets the occlusion-front gate [0x50b8]; special4==0xd sets the deep-span gate [0x5050]; special4==0xe sets the side-emit gate [0x50ab]. The shape code (4..0xe) is written into the per-(depth,slot) walltype array [0x5220] and fed to wall_emit_quad 0x406c / wall_emit_corner 0x45b4.

evidence.details: 0x3be5: `cmp ax,0x10; jae 0x3bf2; xchg bx,ax; shl bx,1; jmp word cs:[bx-0x7ed7]`. Table file offset = (0x10000-0x7ed7)-0x4564 = 0x3bc5 (overlay delta 0x4564). Decoded 16 entries -> targets 0x3b0c(code5)/0x3b14(code6)/0x3b1c(code8)/0x3b24(code9)/0x3b2c(code0xe)/0x3b34(gate[0x50b8])/0x3b51(code4)/0x3b59(code7)/0x3b61(code0xa)/0x3b69(code0xb)/0x3b71(code0xc)/0x3b78(code0xd)/0x3b7f(gate[0x5050])/0x3b9b(gate[0x50ab]); special4=0 -> 0x3bf2 (default no-op). The shape-code writers at 0x3b0c.. each `mov [bp-4], <code>`.

findings.claim: The FOUNTAIN is special4 == 7 (shape code 4): a 4-cell column at gx126 gy118..121 in level-0 region 0 (cellB 6, cellA 2..5), all orient2 == 0 (so it decorates the facing-0/north face). It is the repeated side-wall fixture immediately to the LEFT of the entry corridor (gx127 column) as the party enters facing north — the wall the player walks PAST, matching the user's lived recollection of 'fountains'. special4==7 is the most common SIDE-wall decoration code in region 0 (9 cells level-wide). The other common decorations: special4==1 (code 5) and special4==3 (code 8) are the alcove/recess fixtures; the door/portcullis at a corridor end is a DOOR-edge re-classification (wall field 3), a separate path from special4.

evidence.details: Region-0 special4 column: (cellA2,cellB6)=gx126gy118 sp7; (3,6)=gx126gy119 sp7; (4,6)=gx126gy120 sp7; (5,6)=gx126gy121 sp7. generateDecorations({gx127,gy121,f0}) detects this column on the LEFT slot at depth 0 (shape code 4). The maze-corridor engine fixture (tools/parity/fixtures/engine/maze-corridor.png) is exactly this view (gx127 gy121 f0) and shows the side-wall decoration; it composes to 99.909% via the wired generateFullCallList path. Eyeballed pokeview framebuffers (probe-maze-poke.ts) confirm the entry corridor renders these side fixtures.

findings.claim: The decoration SELECTION (which cell decorates at which facing + the shape code) is now pinned byte-exact and generated. The shape-code -> mazedata.ega placement-INDEX translation is NOT pinned: it runs through the span-flush piece table (0x36e4) inside wall_emit_quad 0x406c (e.g. code 4 emits via span_append 0x3f8d @0x41a9 with a per-depth-indexed source [bx+0x52]), the same decompiler-resistant path the side-wall extent law documents as residue (maze-wall-family-seeding.json). For the canonical maze-corridor view the fountain column's near-wall placements are ALREADY emitted by the near-flank masked-mirror family (generateNearFlankMasked: 13->4 4->13 10->7 7->10), so the view reaches 99.9% without a separate decoration OR-blit — the residual 18px is the deep-door-center detail.

evidence.details: generateCallist(v1) vs the v1 capture (docs/re/findings/maze-views/v1-gy121f0.json) diff: the only captured-but-not-generated indices are {4,7,10,13} which generateFullCallList already emits as the masked near-flank set (4->13,7->10,10->7,13->4) — NO missing OR decoration placement in this view. wall_emit_quad 0x4197 (code 4) -> 0x3f8d span_append with base [bp+4]+0xa and per-depth source [bx+0x52]; 0x3f8d writes the span list @0x50d0 indexed by span count @0x50ce, piece bytes from [bx+0x36e4].

findings.claim: EYEBALL (navreach + view-case fixtures): the level-0 wall DECORATIONS DO render, as ornate WALL-MOUNTED FIXTURES — a vertical white/grey column (pillar/pipe) topped by a yellow FLAME with a green-and-gold ornate BASIN/bracket in the middle. This is consistent with the user's lived recollection of 'fountains' (a wall fountain: a flame-lit ornate basin set into the wall), and it is the recurring decoration the party passes in the entry corridor. CORRECTION/CAVEAT to the 'fountain-identification' finding: the rendered decorations do NOT cleanly correlate with generateDecorations' SLOT attribution. In view-case-09 (gx127 gy123 f0) the ornate fixture renders on the FRONT wall (depth 0), but generateDecorations attributes that view's only decoration to the LEFT slot (gx126 gy123, special4==3 -> code 8) while marking the front cell sp0 — so the model's cell->slot/face geometry is OFFSET vs the rendered placement. In view-case-11 (gx126 gy121 f0, model: FRONT sp7 fountain) the SAME flame+green-basin fixture DOES render (on the near-left + a smaller back-wall flame), confirming sp7 cells carry this fixture. In view-case-05 (gx126 gy121 f3) the sp7 cell's decoration shows as a vertical column of red/orange pixels at the far wall edge (the side-face form). NET: the decoration SELECTION (which cells are special4!=0) is real and the fixtures render; the SHAPE (flame + green-gold basin = plausible wall fountain) is eyeball-confirmed; but the precise special4-value -> fixture-graphic and the cell->screen-slot/face mapping are NOT yet pinned (the slot-attribution offset + the unsolved placement-index emission).

evidence.details: Zoomed (6x) viewport crops in docs/re/findings/maze-views/: decoration-front-fixture-gx127gy123-f0-zoom.png (the flame+green-gold basin on a front wall), decoration-sp7-front-gx126gy121-f0-zoom.png (same fixture, sp7 front view), decoration-sp7-side-gx126gy121-f3-zoom.png (sp7 side-face = red/orange column at the wall edge), navreach-fountain-gx127gy121-f0.png (the committed maze-fountain fixture). All from fixtures captured by REAL moves (navreach cold-boot walk + the nightly-core view-case replay), not poke-recompose. The cell special4/orient2 planes per view are in the _case-analysis dump (in the run log).

unresolved: The shape-code (4..0xe) -> mazedata.ega placement-index mapping is the span-flush residue (0x36e4 piece table / wall_emit_quad). Pinning it byte-exact needs a depth-keyed LIVE build trace of a decoration-facing view. The navreach harness (docs/re/findings/maze-navreach.json) confirmed a real party MOVE DOES re-run the build loop (span count [0x50ce] changes per cell step, unlike poke-recompose=0), but on the patched trace core: (a) the build-loop emit STORES are not observable via the memory write-watch (logs 0 even on a real move whose span count changed), and (b) the scripted gate-entry walk locks the TURN keys, so the party can only walk the gx127 entry column NORTH and never turn to face a decorated cell head-on — and committed turnable states don't unserialize on the patched core. So the placement law stays unpinned; the next attempt should trap an INSTRUCTION trace at wall_emit_quad 0x406c / span_append 0x3f8d on a fresh real-move frame (reading the per-hit stack args) rather than a write-watch.

The generateDecorations cell->slot/face mapping has a GEOMETRY OFFSET vs the rendered placement (eyeball finding decoration-visual-eyeball-2026-06-08): view-case-09 renders the ornate fixture on the FRONT wall but the model attributes that view's decoration to the LEFT slot (and marks the front cell sp0). The model's SELECTION (cells with special4!=0) is right but the per-view slot/face it reports does not match where the engine draws the fixture. Re-deriving the slot/face from the live build loop (see above) would resolve both this and the placement-index law together.

The orient2==facing gate uses orient2 DIRECTLY for the FRONT/side classifier (0x3828, 0x3af1) but the CORNER classifier (0x3c11/0x3dce) uses (orient2+1)%4==facing (0x3d5b) — the two gates differ. generateDecorations models the front/side gate; corner decorations (if any level-0 cell decorates a corner edge) are not yet modeled.

The door/portcullis at a corridor end (wall field 1/3) is re-classified to a shape code via a path SEPARATE from special4 (the maze-corridor front slot is code 8 even though the forward cells have special4==0). That door-orientation re-classification is not part of this decoration-selection crack.
